fact: Digital minister Cina Lawson announced on 1 October 2026 a cooperation under which Kyrgyzstan is to transmit satellite earth-observation data to Togo, with training and technology transfer, to improve agricultural productivity among other uses.

The Togo AI Lab, run by the digital-transformation ministry with UC Berkeley, uses satellite imagery to track agricultural plots and is building models to forecast annual maize and sorghum production, per the funder FID.

The agriculture ministry states that, with FSRP support, ANAMET has been equipped with a satellite-image reception antenna and now accesses satellite data used for the agro-hydro-climatic forecasts it prepares each year for farmers and planners.

The Togo Data Lab, with Togo's Ministry of Agriculture, is developing a project using satellite images, ground data and AI to support farmers, looking at land use, crop yields and soil fertility (Berkeley News).

The Togolese government portal reports a UNDP and Japan project, implemented by Solafune, to build a digital platform combining satellite and field data for crop monitoring, currently tested over a 1,000 km2 pilot zone in Cinkasse and Tone prefectures, Savanes region.

fact: Togo's ministry for public service efficiency and digital transformation announced a space cooperation with Kyrgyzstan launched on 1 October 2026, under which Kyrgyz satellite data will be supplied and local staff trained to use it for crop and pasture monitoring, drought detection and yield estimates.

Togo First reports that since September 2026 a UNDP and Japan supported project is testing satellite data and AI for crop monitoring and climate risk anticipation in the Savanes region, over 1,000 km2 in Cinkasse and Tone prefectures.

fact: ANAMET's agro-hydro-meteorological bulletin of the multidisciplinary working group (GTP), No. 001 of 2026, includes a vegetation-condition section giving VCI and VHI derived from NDVI, rated by prefecture, with the VHI map sourced to GIEWS.
